action: No action needed; for awareness. Election offices and campaigns can use the report to check their own DDoS, web-application and email protections.
exec: Election systems were probed far more often for web flaws than knocked offline, so internal systems and data are the risk to plan for.
plain: Cloudflare reviewed attacks on U.S. election-related websites around the 2026 midterms. It saw no significant DDoS on Election Day, but many attempts to exploit website flaws.

key_findings: No significant DDoS attack across about 1,400 election-related sites on November 3; the only significant one was on November 2 against a California U.S. House candidate, at 520,000 requests.
Government election sites faced website vulnerability attempts 180 times more often than DDoS.

Cloudflare mitigated 392 million website vulnerability attacks on government election sites in the 12 months before the election; exploit attempts rose from 200,000 per day in January to 2 million per day in October.
Largest single DDoS on civil society and journalism: 3.04 billion requests against a U.S. news organization on September 10, 2026.
3.9% of emails to Cloudflare for Campaigns organizations were malicious in the 90 days before the election.

summary: Cloudflare published its review of internet traffic and attacks around the 2026 U.S. midterm elections. It recorded no significant DDoS across about 1,400 election-related sites on Election Day, while government election sites faced vulnerability-exploit attempts 180 times more often than DDoS. The figures are the vendor's own, from its network.
title: Cloudflare: election sites saw many web-exploit attempts but no significant Election Day DDoS in 2026 midterms

validation.note: Cloudflare's own report; figures are the vendor's and not independently confirmed.

review.note: Re-read Cloudflare post: 1,400 sites, no significant DDoS 3 Nov, 520,000 on 2 Nov, 180x, 392M, 200k to 2M per day, 3.04B on 10 Sep, 3.9% malicious email, published 19 Nov
